name: Sertraline
metabolism: Initial N-demethylation forms less active N-desmethylsertraline. Further deamination, reduction, hydroxylation and glucuronidation precede elimination in urine and feces. Multiple enzymes participate; the reviewed label does not identify one exclusive CYP pathway.
summary: Sertraline is a selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor used to treat major depression and several anxiety-related disorders.
toxicities: Warns about suicidal thoughts and behaviour in pediatric and young adult patients, serotonin syndrome, increased bleeding, QTc prolongation, hyponatremia, seizures, mania and hypomania, and discontinuation syndrome.
Common adverse reactions listed for sertraline include nausea, diarrhea/loose stool, tremor, dyspepsia, decreased appetite, sweating, and sexual dysfunction.
generalRisks: The label is specifically oral sertraline capsules (revised 2026-01); available capsule strengths are 150 mg and 200 mg and the label does not cover every sertraline product’s initiation/titration instructions. About suicidality, serotonin syndrome, bleeding, QTc prolongation, hyponatremia, seizures, mania/hypomania and withdrawal symptoms.
saferUse: Monitor for worsening mood or suicidal thoughts, especially in younger people and after changes. Seek urgent care for suspected serotonin syndrome or seizure.
Do not stop suddenly; the label advises gradual dose reduction and monitoring for discontinuation symptoms.
Do not combine with MAOIs or pimozide. Check with a clinician before combining with serotonergic medicines, QT-prolonging medicines, NSAIDs, aspirin, warfarin, or other anticoagulants.
dosageRemark: The label is a prescription oral capsule label and specifies capsule strengths of 150 mg and 200 mg; these therapeutic instructions are not recreational dose guidance. Do not transfer them to other sertraline formulations.
